title: Print the next slice id without allocating it
lead:
There is no command that answers "what id comes next?" `add` and `import`
learn it only by calling `ids.allocate`, which also increments
`index.next_id` (`src/slicer/ids.py`, ~lines 70-84). The stored mark is
already there: `format_id(prefix, next_id, width)`. A caller who wants the
number before creating an item has to read `.slicer/index.json`, which
agents are told not to do.

The name to ship is `slicer next-id`, beside `next`. `gen-new-id` does not
match the other commands.
findings_note: user request for a next-id command
boundary: **Not in this slice:** reserving the id. This command does not bump `next_id` and does not create an item. Two callers can still be handed the same id; claiming it stays on `add` and `import`.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Scripts and agents plan a follow-up (`add --id`, a branch name, a depends
line) before any item exists. They need the formatted id the project would
hand out, from the index's own prefix and width. Reading the counter and
formatting it by hand drifts from `allocate`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ids.py` — a read of the next formatted id that does not call `allocate`
- `src/slicer/cli.py` — the `next-id` command, next to `next` (~line 1002)
- `README.md` — the command table, on the `next` row (~line 116)
- `docs/agents.md` — the command payload table
- `tests/test_cli.py` or `tests/test_ids.py`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. A fresh project prints `S01`. `next_id` in the index stays 1, and a second call prints `S01` again.
2. After one `add`, it prints `S02` and the index is unchanged by the call.
3. `--json` returns `{"id": "S02"}` and nothing else. The text form is the bare id, so a script can capture it.
4. A project whose prefix or width differs (`TASK-`, width 3) gets that format, for example `TASK-007`.
5. When `next_id` would reuse an existing id, the command exits 3 with `code="corrupt"` and writes nothing, the same refusal `allocate` already makes.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add a function that formats `index.next_id` with `index.id_prefix` and `index.id_width`, checks `require_valid`, and raises the existing `corrupt` error when that id is already in the index. It must not increment `next_id` and must not call `allocate`, because `allocate` consumes the id.

`slicer next-id` is read-only: no lock, no log entry, no `--render`. Text prints the id alone. `--json` prints `{"id": "..."}`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `slicer next-id` on this repo prints the formatted id for the current `next_id`, and `slicer check` still passes with an unchanged index.
